methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective Korean health-screening cohort (NHIS-HEALS, 131,167 participants with prehypertension). Clear exposure definition (JNC 7 prehypertension criteria). Blood pressure trajectories classified at baseline and follow-up (2003-2006). Landmark approach to reduce immortal time bias. Cause-specific Cox models with competing risks. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses conducted (exposure windows, lag times, BP reclassification per ACC/AHA and ESC 2024). Limitations: retrospective, observational, confounding by indication (antihypertensive choice).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Addresses clinically relevant question: does prehypertension progression increase GI cancer risk? Findings directly applicable to cancer prevention and hypertension management. Identifies high-risk groups for enhanced surveillance. Requires prospective validation.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive STROBE adherence: objectives, cohort selection with explicit inclusion/exclusion, baseline characteristics, outcome definitions with ICD-10 codes, statistical methods (landmark approach, cause-specific Cox, FDR notation). Sensitivity analyses robust. NHIS data are semi-public with authorization. Minor gap: no pre-registration.

novelty_literature.justification: Hypertension-cancer associations previously studied. Prehypertension-specific analysis adds novelty. Blood pressure trajectory approach novel for cancer prediction.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized with clear problem framing. Methods detailed including landmark approach and competing risks handling. Results logically presented with Kaplan-Meier curves and forest plots. Limitations candidly discussed. Discussion contextualizes findings within hypertension and cancer literature.

key_strengths: Large prospective cohort of 131,167 prehypertensive individuals with 13-year follow-up enabling long-term GI cancer incidence assessment
Rigorous statistical methodology: landmark approach reducing immortal time bias, cause-specific Cox models accounting for competing risks, FDR correction for multiple comparisons
Comprehensive sensitivity analyses with multiple BP reclassification systems (ACC/AHA 2017, ESC 2024) strengthening generalizability
key_concerns: Observational design subject to confounding by indication (antihypertensive drug choice influenced by unmeasured factors); medication adherence analysis partially addresses but not comprehensive
Administrative database lacks granular data on screening, treatment adherence (MPR proxy), lifestyle factors (diet, exercise beyond self-report)
Site-specific findings (colorectal, pancreatic) stronger than overall; esophageal marginally significant; heterogeneous effects require careful interpretation
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid observational cohort study with rigorous statistical methodology (landmark, competing risks, sensitivity analyses) identifying progression to hypertension as GI cancer risk factor. Tier 3 appropriate for well-conducted epidemiological research requiring prospective validation.
